title: Recording: Hi, Hi, Hi by Wings | 1972
content:
Studio Two, EMI Studios, London
Producer: Paul McCartney
Engineer: John Leckie

Wings recorded the backing track for ‘Hi, Hi, Hi’ on 20 September 1972.

It came after five unsuccessful sessions, which involved overdubs onto a live recording, and various studio takes that were deemed unsatisfactory.

On this day Paul McCartney decided to start afresh once again. Ten takes of a rhythm track, numbered 52-61 were recorded, only five were complete. They had McCartney on bass guitar, Denny Laine on rhythm guitar, and Denny Seiwell on drums.

Take 61 was considered the best, although it required an edit towards the end to fix an error. Onto the backing track they then added seven electric guitar tracks, two more played through a Leslie rotating speaker, double-tracked lead vocals, and piano.

Studio engineer John Leckie then made a rough mix, so McCartney could consider what else the song required. ‘Hi, Hi, Hi’ was by no means finished, but it had taken a significant step closer.

Page last updated: 24 November 2025
